one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent correctly solved the optimization problem but saved the final result as a binary numpy file (solution_refined.npy) instead of the text file solution.txt expected by the evaluator, because it never considered what output format or filename the benchmark requires.
t_err_evidence: In step 2 the agent writes optimize.py with 'np.save("solution.npy", result.x)' — the first code artifact already commits to binary .npy format and ignores the requirement to produce a solution.txt text file.
t_commit_evidence: In step 19 refine.py is executed and produces solution_refined.npy as the final artifact. After this the agent never creates solution.txt; the wrong output file is now the only candidate to be evaluated.
trigger_explanation: The agent never investigated what file the evaluator/pytest expects. The task description says 'give me a high-quality solution' without specifying a filename, but the benchmark's evaluator implicitly requires solution.txt (as shown by the reference solution using np.savetxt('solution.txt', x_val)). The agent defaulted to numpy's binary save format and a self-chosen filename without ever checking the evaluation harness.
